question.text: A ball weighing 100 N sits at rest on a rough slope tilted 30° from the horizontal; a horizontal cord, running from a point A on the ball to a fixed point B on the slope, keeps the ball from sliding down. Work out the following three quantities.

parts.label: a
parts.asks: Find the tension in the cord.

parts.label: b
parts.asks: Find the friction force acting on the ball.

parts.label: c
parts.asks: Find the normal reaction the slope exerts on the ball.

conditions: a horizontal cord AB (A on the ball, B fixed on the incline) holds the ball stationary

figure.description: An inclined surface rises from the ground at an angle of 30°. A ball rests on this sloped surface, its centre marked C. A horizontal cord runs from point A, the topmost point of the ball (directly above its centre C), to point B, a fixed point on the incline surface farther up the slope at the same height as A, so the cord itself is horizontal and tangent to the ball at A.

solution.approach: Weight and normal reaction pass through the sphere's centre, so balancing moments there for the tension and friction gives one relation, and force balance gives the rest.

steps.text: The string AB is horizontal and tied where it touches the sphere without cutting into it, so A is the topmost point of the sphere; there the radius to A is vertical, at height r above the centre C.
steps.equation: moment arm of T about C = r

steps.text: Friction f acts at the contact point with the incline, tangent to the sphere there, which is also always at a perpendicular distance r from the centre.
steps.equation: moment arm of f about C = r

steps.text: The weight acts at the centre and the normal reaction acts along the radius through the contact point, so both pass through C and add no moment; balancing the moments of T and f about C then requires them to be equal.
steps.why_this_step: With only T and f having a nonzero moment arm about the centre, and the sphere in equilibrium, their moments must cancel, which — since both arms equal r — makes the two forces equal.

steps.text: Resolve all forces horizontally and vertically: weight w down, normal reaction N perpendicular to the 30° incline, friction f up the incline, tension T horizontal.
steps.equation: horizontal: T − N sin30° + f cos30° = 0;  vertical: N cos30° + f sin30° = w

steps.text: Substitute f = T into both equations and solve.
steps.equation: T(1+cos30°) = N sin30°;  N cos30° + T sin30° = w

steps.text: Solve the two equations for T and N.

final_answer.value: (a) tension T = 100(2−√3) N ≈ 26.8 N. (b) friction f = 100(2−√3) N ≈ 26.8 N, acting up the incline. (c) normal reaction N = 100 N

common_mistakes.text: Treating the sphere as frictionless and solving only T − N sin30° = 0 and N cos30° = w gives the wrong N ≈ 115.5 N and T ≈ 57.7 N, missing the incline's friction.
Writing only the two force-balance equations and stopping, because T, f and N are three unknowns; the third equation is the moment balance about the centre, which gives f = T.
